title: Make it beautiful: Post-processing
description: Add a Post-process Volume, then tonemapping, glow, volumetric fog, sun shafts and moving clouds.

steps.title: Select the Effects object
steps.text: This scene looks plain on purpose. Click Effects in the Hierarchy. This empty object will hold the look of the scene.

steps.title: Add a Post-process Volume
steps.text: In the Inspector, click Add Component, type Post and pick Post-process Volume. It changes how the camera image looks.

steps.title: Turn on Tonemapping
steps.text: Tick the box next to Tonemapping. It turns very bright light into nice screen colours, like a film camera.

steps.title: Add Bloom and Color
steps.text: Tick Bloom so bright things glow. Then tick Color Adjustments and play with Contrast and Saturation.

steps.title: Turn on Volumetric Fog
steps.text: Tick Fog. Inside it, keep Volumetric ticked: now the fog catches the sunlight.

steps.title: Glow toward the sun
steps.text: Drag Anisotropy to the right, to about 0.7. Light now scatters forward, so the fog glows when you look at the sun.

steps.title: Keep the fog low
steps.text: Base Height is where the fog starts to thin out. Above Maximum Height it is gone. Try a Maximum Height of 15.

steps.title: Add Sun Shafts
steps.text: Tick Sun Shafts (Screen). When the sun is on screen, bright rays now shine out around it. Intensity sets how strong they are.

steps.title: Add Volumetric Clouds
steps.text: Tick Volumetric Clouds. Pick a Preset, like Sparse or Stormy, then move Coverage to add or remove clouds.

steps.title: Shape the clouds
steps.text: Fluffy ↔ Sharp turns soft edges into crisp ones. Under Wind, Direction and Speed set where and how fast the clouds drift.

steps.title: Scene view effects
steps.text: This ☁ button turns fog, clouds and effects on or off in the Scene view while you work. The arrow next to it picks which ones.

steps.title: Press Play
steps.text: Press Play to watch the clouds move with the wind. Press it again to stop. Well done!
